findings.summary: Unauthenticated remote memory exhaustion: unbounded widget-state, session table, and request bodies from client-controlled input
findings.description:
## Affected

`github.com/malcolmston/streamlit` **<= 0.3.0** (all published versions). No fix released.

Parity case: `widget-hidden-then-shown` (group `widget-values`, `parity/streamlit/`).
Oracle: PyPI `streamlit==1.61.1` via `AppTest`.

The non-sensitive correctness half of the same root cause - hidden widgets keeping stale
values - remains tracked publicly as `Malcolmston/streamlit#9`. The resource-exhaustion half
below was moved here.

## Upstream vs port

Widget state is never pruned. The released `Session` in v0.3.0 has **no `seen` set and no
`pruneStaleWidgets`** at all. The widget-state map is keyed by **client-supplied strings**
taken from the body of `POST /api/run`, and entries are never removed, so every unknown key a
client sends is retained for the life of the session.

Upstream Streamlit discards widget state once a widget stops being rendered, which bounds the
map to the widgets the script actually draws.

## Impact (attacker terms)

Untrusted input drives unbounded server-side memory growth, with no cap and no eviction.
Anyone who can reach `POST /api/run` can add arbitrarily many keys to their session's map, and
they persist for the session's lifetime; repeating across sessions multiplies the footprint
until the process is OOM-killed. This is denial of service / resource exhaustion only - no
confidentiality or integrity impact, no code execution, no cross-tenant data exposure. The
library's own `API-DEVIATIONS.md` already identifies this shape for the data cache ("An
unbounded cache whose keys derive from user input grows until the process dies"); the widget
map has the same shape and no such bound.

## Reproduction

`POST /api/run` with `{"state":{"<random-key-1>":1, "<random-key-2>":1, ...}}` grows the
session map by one entry per unknown key, permanently - no request rejects the unknown keys
and nothing later removes them.

That no pruning happens at all is independently observable through the correctness symptom:

```go
func app(s *st.Session) {
	if s.Checkbox("show", true, "show") {
		s.TextInput("Name", "ada", "name")
	}
}
```

Set `name` to `"grace"`, uncheck `show`, re-check it: the port returns `"grace"` where
upstream 1.61.1 returns the declared default `"ada"`.

## Suggested fix

Prune widget state to the set of widgets rendered in the current run **and** reject or bound
keys that no widget has ever declared - pruning by "seen this run" alone still lets
never-rendered client-supplied keys accumulate. Add a hard per-session cap.

Note: the unreleased working tree already adds a `seen` set and `pruneStaleWidgets`, which
addresses the stale-value half; the unknown-key growth half must be verified explicitly
against that change before it is relied on as a fix.

## Severity rationale

Graded **low**: real, untrusted-input-driven and unauthenticated - but availability only,
scoped to the memory of sessions the attacker himself opens, and mitigable operationally with
session limits and process memory caps. Deliberately not inflated to match the XSS findings in
the sibling ports.
